THESE APPEAS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM :
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  ORAL JUDGMENT

These appeals are arising out of the common judgment and award dated 02.01.2019 in MVC No.242/2016 and MVC No.243/2016 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Shahapur (for short 'the Tribunal'), allowing the claim petitions and awarding compensation to the claimants.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties would be referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. The facts as averred by the claimants are that, on 25.09.2015, the deceased Suvarna, her daughter- Kumari Sahana and her husband were travelling from from their village Thimmapur/Ranganpet to Kalaburagi in a NEKRTC bus bearing No.KA-32/F-1678 and around The Nekrtc Division Yadgir vs Mallappa And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153037478/
6 12.15 p.m., when the bus reached near Surpur-Shahapur main road at Kongadi bridge, the driver of the bus drove the NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER same in a negligent manner and as such, the deceased Suvarna, who was sitting in the rear seat of the bus came near the door, as her child Sahana has urinated and as there was a road breaker, the driver of the bus suddenly applied the break and on account of the same, the deceased Suvarna and her child fell down from the bus and thereafter, they have been taken to Hathigudar Primary Health Center for first aid and thereafter, they have been taken to Shahapur Government Hospital for further treatment.
It is also stated that, they have been taken to Ganga Multi Specialty Hospital at Kalaburagi and thereafter taken to a hospital at Raichur for further treatment and died in the way to the hospital.

entities.text: Ganga Multi Specialty Hospital at Kalaburagi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Thereafter,
the father of the deceased Suvarna lodged the complaint on 02.12.2015 before the Shahapur Police Station, Yadagir District and the same was registered in Crime No.303/2015.
Hence, the claimants have preferred MVC No.242/2016 and MVC No.243/2016 before the Tribunal, seeking compensation.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER
4. On service of notice, respondent No.3- Corporation entered appearance and filed detailed written statement, denying the involvement of the vehicle as well as the accident.

It is the case of the respondent- Corporation that, when the said Suvarna was sitting in the bus, there was a quarrel between deceased Suvarna with her husband-Mallappa and the same was continued and immediately, the said Suvarna along with the child, opened the door and jumped from the bus.

Therefore, it is the case of the respondent-Corporation that, the alleged complaint was lodged after two months from the date of incident, which makes it clear that, the claimants are seeking compensation fraudulently and accordingly, sought for dismissal of the claim petitions.
5. In order to prove their case, the claimants have examined two witnesses as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked 38 documents as Exs.P1 to P38.

On the other hand, the respondents have examined four witnesses as RWs.1 to 4 and got marked 09 documents as Exs.R1 to R9.

7 6.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal, after considering the material on record, by judgment and award dated 02.01.2019,
awarded compensation of Rs.12,01,200/- in MVC No.242/2016 and Rs.2,00,000/- in MVC No.243/2016 with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petitions till realization and directed the respondent No.3-Corporaiton to the deposit the same.
7. Feeling aggrieved by the inadequacy of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants have preferred MFA Nos.202130/2019 and 202171/2019, seeking enhancement of compensation.
Whereas, the Corporation has filed MFA Nos.200974/2019 and 200975/2019, challenging the liability.
8. I have heard, Sri Sharanabasappa M. Patil, learned counsel appearing for the Corporation and Sri S.V. Paraddy, learned counsel appearing for the claimants.

9. Learned counsel appearing for the Corporation contended that, the Tribunal has failed to consider the fact - 11 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER that, there was delay of nearly three months in lodging the complaint and also the proper reasons have not been made by the claimants as to the delay in lodging the complaint and accordingly,
sought for interference of this Court.

It is further contended by the learned counsel appearing for the Corporation that, the deceased herself along with her child jumped from the moving bus and committed suicide for her personal agony with her husband, who was also sitting in the bus.
Therefore, there was no negligence on the part of the driver or conductor of the bus in question.
Accordingly, sought for interference of this Court.
It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the Corporation that, the award of compensation is on the higher side, which requires to be reduced.

10. Per contra, Sri S.V. Paraddy, learned counsel appearing for the claimants sought to justify the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal as to the finding that the alleged accident occurred solely on the - 12 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 The Nekrtc Division Yadgir vs Mallappa And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153037478/
8 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER negligence on the part of the driver of the bus in question.

entities.text: Nekrtc Division Yadgir vs Mallappa And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the claimants that, the award of compensation is meager, which requires to be enhanced.

11. In order to buttress his arguments, learned counsel appearing for the claimants places reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sanju Bai Prajapati & Ors. vs. The New India Assurance Company Ltd. & Ors. reported in 2025 INSC 823 and argued that, the delay in lodging the complaint cannot be a ground for denying compensation to the claimant and therefore,
sought for interference of this Court.

entities.text: Sanju Bai Prajapati & Ors. vs. The New India Assurance Company Ltd. & Ors. reported in 2025 INSC 823
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In the light of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, I have carefully examined the finding recorded by Tribunal and also the documents produced by the parties.

A careful examination of the finding recorded by the Tribunal would indicate that, the alleged accident was occurred on 25.09.2025 around - 13 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER 12.15 p.m., wherein the deceased Suvarna and her child Kumari Sahana as well as the husband of deceased Suvarna namely, Mallappa were travelling in the NEKRTC bus bearing No.KA-32/F-1678 from Thimmapur village towards Kalaburagi.
It is also stated in the claim petition that, when the bus was moving near the bridge in between Surpur-Shahapur, the deceased along with the child came near the door of the bus.
In this regard, it is pertinent to mention here that, Ex.P2-complaint was lodged by the father of the deceased Suvarna.

It is to be noted that, if the alleged accident has really occurred, nothing has prevented the husband of the deceased Suvarna i.e., Mallappa, who was also travelling in the bus, from lodging the complaint immediately to the jurisdictional police and it is also not in dispute that, there was a delay in lodging the complaint for a period of 68 days.
The said complaint is lodged by the father of the deceased and not the husband of the deceased and the said aspect has been ignored by the Tribunal.

It is also to be noted that, nothing - 14 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 The Nekrtc Division Yadgir vs Mallappa And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153037478/
9 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER is forthcoming from the records as to why the deceased came near the door, which was closed and that apart, the argument of the learned counsel appearing for the claimants is that, as there was a speed breaker in the road, suddenly the bus was slowed down and on account of the same, the door was opened and as the deceased Suvarna was standing near the door, fell down from the bus along with the child.

entities.text: Nekrtc Division Yadgir vs Mallappa And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said argument cannot be accepted as to the occurrence of the accident, as the husband of the deceased Suvarna, who was sitting in the bus himself ought to have taken further steps for lodging the complaint immediately and undisputedly, the delay in lodging the complaint is more than two months.
It is also to be noted that, though the MLC intimation was sent according to Ex.P23, however, as the respondent- Corporation had denied the occurrence of the accident,
nothing
has prevented the claimants from examining the police authorities or the hospital authorities as to sending the MLC intimation to the police.

The said fact makes it - 15 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER clear that, the claimants have created the documents for the purpose of getting compensation and that too, the perusal of the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 makes it clear that, the claimants have created the documents, which is nothing but a fraud as to secure compensation from the respondent-Corporation.
13.

In that view of the matter, it is relevant to cite the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of Veerappa and Another vs. Siddappa and Another reported in ILR 2009 KAR 3562,
wherein it is held that, fraud and justice never dwell together.

entities.text: Veerappa and Another vs. Siddappa and Another reported in ILR 2009 KAR 3562
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The material on record would also make it clear that, the claimants have played fraud on the Tribunal to get compensation from the respondent-Corporation.

The claimants have failed to prove as to the delay in lodging the complaint for a period of more than two months, so also, the evidence adduced by the PW.1 and PW.2 cannot be accepted, as PW.1 is the husband of the deceased Suvarna and PW.2 is the father of the deceased Suvarana.
- 16 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER The Nekrtc Division Yadgir vs Mallappa And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153037478/
10 No independent witnesses have been examined as to the occurrence of the accident.

Even if it is assumed for the sake of arguments that the accident has really occurred, definitely, the bus would have been stopped and at least one of the passengers would have been examined by the claimants or the complaint would have been lodged by the conductor or the driver as to the occurrence of the accident.

In that view of the matter, I am of the view that, the Tribunal has committed an error in arriving at a conclusion to answer Issue No.1 holding that, the respondent-Corporation is liable for their actionable negligence as to the alleged accident.
In that view of the matter, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the Corporation is to be accepted.

14. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.200974/2019 and MFA No.200975/ 2019 filed by the Corporation are allowed.
- 17 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER  ii) MFA No.202130/2019 and MFA No.202171/2019 filed by the claimants are dismissed.
Consequently, the claim petitions in MVC No.242/2016 and MVC No.243/2016 are hereby dismissed.
iii) The amount in deposit made by the Corporation, if any, be refunded to the Corporation on due identification.

Sd/-

opennyai_summary.facts:
Thereafter,
the father of the deceased Suvarna lodged the complaint on 02.12.2015 before the Shahapur Police Station, Yadagir District and the same was registered in Crime No.303/2015.
Hence, the claimants have preferred MVC No.242/2016 and MVC No.243/2016 before the Tribunal, seeking compensation.
Therefore, it is the case of the respondent-Corporation that, the alleged complaint was lodged after two months from the date of incident, which makes it clear that, the claimants are seeking compensation fraudulently and accordingly, sought for dismissal of the claim petitions.
The Tribunal, after considering the material on record, by judgment and award dated 02.01.2019,
awarded compensation of Rs.12,01,200/- in MVC No.242/2016 and Rs.2,00,000/- in MVC No.243/2016 with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petitions till realization and directed the respondent No.3-Corporaiton to the deposit the same.
7. Feeling aggrieved by the inadequacy of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants have preferred MFA Nos.202130/2019 and 202171/2019, seeking enhancement of compensation.
Whereas, the Corporation has filed MFA Nos.200974/2019 and 200975/2019, challenging the liability.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
10. Per contra, Sri S.V. Paraddy, learned counsel appearing for the claimants sought to justify the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal as to the finding that the alleged accident occurred solely on the - 12 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 The Nekrtc Division Yadgir vs Mallappa And Ors on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153037478/
8 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER negligence on the part of the driver of the bus in question.
11. In order to buttress his arguments, learned counsel appearing for the claimants places reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sanju Bai Prajapati & Ors. vs. The New India Assurance Company Ltd. & Ors. reported in 2025 INSC 823 and argued that, the delay in lodging the complaint cannot be a ground for denying compensation to the claimant and therefore,
sought for interference of this Court.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The said complaint is lodged by the father of the deceased and not the husband of the deceased and the said aspect has been ignored by the Tribunal.
has prevented the claimants from examining the police authorities or the hospital authorities as to sending the MLC intimation to the police.
The said fact makes it - 15 -  NC: 2026:KHC-K:1038 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER clear that, the claimants have created the documents for the purpose of getting compensation and that too, the perusal of the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 makes it clear that, the claimants have created the documents, which is nothing but a fraud as to secure compensation from the respondent-Corporation.
13.
The claimants have failed to prove as to the delay in lodging the complaint for a period of more than two months, so also, the evidence adduced by the PW.1 and PW.2 cannot be accepted, as PW.1 is the husband of the deceased Suvarna and PW.2 is the father of the deceased Suvarana.
Even if it is assumed for the sake of arguments that the accident has really occurred, definitely, the bus would have been stopped and at least one of the passengers would have been examined by the claimants or the complaint would have been lodged by the conductor or the driver as to the occurrence of the accident.
In that view of the matter, I am of the view that, the Tribunal has committed an error in arriving at a conclusion to answer Issue No.1 holding that, the respondent-Corporation is liable for their actionable negligence as to the alleged accident.
